questions.question:
A [latex]2^{nd}[/latex] degree polynomial, f(x) has values of 1, 4 and 15 at x = 0, 1 and 2, respectively. The integral [latex]\int_{0}^{2}f(x)dx[/latex] is to be estimated by applying the trapezoidal rule to this data. What is the error (defined as "true value - approximate value")
in the estimate ?
questions.explanation: f(x)=1, 4, 15 at x=0, 1 and 2 respectively [latex]   \int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx =\frac{h}{2}\left ( f_{1}+2f_{2}+f_{3} \right )   [/latex](3 point Trapezoidal Rule) Here  h=1 [latex]\therefore \;\; \int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx=\left ( 1+2\times +15 \right )=12[/latex] [latex]\therefore [/latex] Approximate value by Trapezoidal Rule =12 Since f(x) is second degree polynomial, let, [latex]    \begin{aligned}  f\left ( x \right )&=a_{0}+a_{1}x+a_{2}x^{2} \\      f\left ( 0 \right )&=1 \\ \Rightarrow  \;\; a_{0}+0+0&=1 \\ \Rightarrow   \;\;   a_{0}&=1 \\      f\left ( 1 \right )&=4 \\ \Rightarrow \;\;  a_{0}+a_{1}+a_{2}&=4 \\ \Rightarrow  \;\; 1+a_{1}+a_{2}&=4 \\ \Rightarrow \;\;   a_{1}+a_{2}&=3 \;\;\;...(i)\\      f\left ( 2 \right )&=15 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a_{0}+2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=15 \\ \Rightarrow \;\;1+2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=15 \\ \Rightarrow   \;\; 2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=14 \;\;\; ...(ii) \end{aligned}[/latex] Solving (i) and (ii) [latex]a_{1}=-1[/latex] and [latex]a_{2}=4[/latex], [latex]\therefore  \;\; f\left ( x \right )=1-x+4x^{2}[/latex] Now, exact value of [latex]\begin{aligned} &\int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx \\   &=\int_{0}^{2}\left ( 1-x+4x^{2} \right ) \\   &=\left [ x-\frac{x^{2}}{2}+\frac{4x^{3}}{3} \right ]_{0}^{2}=\frac{32}{3} \end{aligned}[/latex] Error = Exact-Approximate value [latex] =\frac{32}{3}-12=-\frac{4}{3}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
f(x)=1, 4, 15 at x=0, 1 and 2 respectively
[latex] \int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx =\frac{h}{2}\left ( f_{1}+2f_{2}+f_{3} \right ) [/latex](3 point Trapezoidal Rule)
Here h=1
[latex]\therefore \;\; \int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx=\left ( 1+2\times +15 \right )=12[/latex]
[latex]\therefore [/latex] Approximate value by Trapezoidal Rule =12
Since f(x) is second degree polynomial, let,
[latex] \begin{aligned} f\left ( x \right )&=a_{0}+a_{1}x+a_{2}x^{2} \\ f\left ( 0 \right )&=1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a_{0}+0+0&=1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a_{0}&=1 \\ f\left ( 1 \right )&=4 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a_{0}+a_{1}+a_{2}&=4 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; 1+a_{1}+a_{2}&=4 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a_{1}+a_{2}&=3 \;\;\;...(i)\\ f\left ( 2 \right )&=15 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a_{0}+2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=15 \\ \Rightarrow \;\;1+2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=15 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; 2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=14 \;\;\; ...(ii) \end{aligned}[/latex]
Solving (i) and (ii) [latex]a_{1}=-1[/latex] and [latex]a_{2}=4[/latex],
[latex]\therefore \;\; f\left ( x \right )=1-x+4x^{2}[/latex]
Now, exact value of
[latex]\begin{aligned} &\int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx \\ &=\int_{0}^{2}\left ( 1-x+4x^{2} \right ) \\ &=\left [ x-\frac{x^{2}}{2}+\frac{4x^{3}}{3} \right ]_{0}^{2}=\frac{32}{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Error = Exact-Approximate value
[latex] =\frac{32}{3}-12=-\frac{4}{3}[/latex]

taken in counterclockwise direction) [latex]\oint_{c}\frac{z^{3}-6}{3z-i}dz[/latex] is
questions.explanation: Cauchy's integral theorem is, [latex]  \begin{aligned} f\left ( a \right )&=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{c}\, \frac{f\left ( z \right )}{z-a}dz\\ \text{i.e., } \oint_{C}\, \frac{f\left ( z \right )}{z-a}dz&=2\pi i\, f\left ( a \right ) \\ \text{Now, } \oint_{C}\, \frac{z^{3}-6}{3z-i}dz&=\frac{1}{3}\oint_{c}\, \frac{z^{3-6}}{\left ( z-\frac{i}{3} \right )} \end{aligned}[/latex] Applying Cauchy's integral theorem, [latex] \begin{aligned}  &=\frac{1}{3}\left ( 2\pi i\: f\left ( \frac{i}{3} \right ) \right ) \\   &=\frac{1}{3}\left ( 2\pi i\left [ \left ( \frac{i}{3} \right )^{3}-6 \right ] \right ) \\   &=\frac{1}{3}\left [ 2\pi i\left ( \frac{i^{3}}{27}-6 \right ) \right ] \\ &=\frac{2\pi }{81}i^{4}-4\pi i \\   &=\frac{2\pi }{81}-4\pi i \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: The solution of the differential equation, [latex]x^{2} \frac{dy}{dx}+ 2xy - x + 1 = 0[/latex] , given that at x = 1, y = 0 is
questions.explanation: Giiven, [latex]x^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+2xy-x+1=0 \;\; \left ( x=1, y=0 \right ) [/latex] [latex]   x^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+2xy =x-1[/latex] Dividing by [latex]x^{2}[/latex], [latex]   \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+\left ( \frac{2}{x} \right )y =\left ( \frac{x-1}{x^{2}} \right )[/latex] which is a linear first order differential equation of the form, [latex]   \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+Py =Q[/latex] [latex] \begin{aligned} \text{Integrating factor}&=I.F=e^{\int Pdx}=e^{\int \frac{2}{x}dx} \\     &=e^{2\log x} \\     &=e^{\log_{e}x^{2}}=x^{2} \\   y\times I.F&=\int Q\left ( I.F \right )dx \\    y.x^{2}&=\int \left ( \frac{x-1}{x^{2}} \right ).x^{2}.dx \\     &=\int \left ( x-1 \right )dx \\    yx^{2}&=\frac{x^{2}}{2}-x+C \\ \text{Now at }x=1, \;y=0,\\ \text{i.e. }   0\times 1^{2}&=\frac{1^{2}}{2}-1+C \\     0&=\frac{1}{2}-1+C \\     C&=\frac{1}{2} \\ \therefore \;\;  yx^{2}&=\frac{x^{2}}{2}-x+\frac{1}{2} \\   y&=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{2x^{2}} \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Giiven, [latex]x^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+2xy-x+1=0 \;\; \left ( x=1, y=0 \right ) [/latex]
[latex] x^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+2xy =x-1[/latex]
Dividing by [latex]x^{2}[/latex],
[latex] \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+\left ( \frac{2}{x} \right )y =\left ( \frac{x-1}{x^{2}} \right )[/latex]
which is a linear first order differential equation of the form,
[latex] \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+Py =Q[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text{Integrating factor}&=I.F=e^{\int Pdx}=e^{\int \frac{2}{x}dx} \\ &=e^{2\log x} \\ &=e^{\log_{e}x^{2}}=x^{2} \\ y\times I.F&=\int Q\left ( I.F \right )dx \\ y.x^{2}&=\int \left ( \frac{x-1}{x^{2}} \right ).x^{2}.dx \\ &=\int \left ( x-1 \right )dx \\ yx^{2}&=\frac{x^{2}}{2}-x+C \\ \text{Now at }x=1, \;y=0,\\ \text{i.e. } 0\times 1^{2}&=\frac{1^{2}}{2}-1+C \\ 0&=\frac{1}{2}-1+C \\ C&=\frac{1}{2} \\ \therefore \;\; yx^{2}&=\frac{x^{2}}{2}-x+\frac{1}{2} \\ y&=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{2x^{2}} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question:
A [latex]2^{nd}[/latex] degree polynomial, f(x) has values of 1, 4 and 15 at x = 0, 1 and 2, respectively. The integral [latex]\int_{0}^{2}f(x)dx[/latex] is to be estimated by applying the trapezoidal rule to this data. What is the error (defined as "true value - approximate value")
in the estimate ?
questions.explanation: f(x)=1, 4, 15 at x=0, 1 and 2 respectively [latex]   \int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx =\frac{h}{2}\left ( f_{1}+2f_{2}+f_{3} \right )   [/latex](3 point Trapezoidal Rule) Here  h=1 [latex]\therefore \;\; \int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx=\left ( 1+2\times +15 \right )=12[/latex] [latex]\therefore [/latex] Approximate value by Trapezoidal Rule =12 Since f(x) is second degree polynomial, let, [latex]    \begin{aligned}  f\left ( x \right )&=a_{0}+a_{1}x+a_{2}x^{2} \\      f\left ( 0 \right )&=1 \\ \Rightarrow  \;\; a_{0}+0+0&=1 \\ \Rightarrow   \;\;   a_{0}&=1 \\      f\left ( 1 \right )&=4 \\ \Rightarrow \;\;  a_{0}+a_{1}+a_{2}&=4 \\ \Rightarrow  \;\; 1+a_{1}+a_{2}&=4 \\ \Rightarrow \;\;   a_{1}+a_{2}&=3 \;\;\;...(i)\\      f\left ( 2 \right )&=15 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a_{0}+2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=15 \\ \Rightarrow \;\;1+2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=15 \\ \Rightarrow   \;\; 2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=14 \;\;\; ...(ii) \end{aligned}[/latex] Solving (i) and (ii) [latex]a_{1}=-1[/latex] and [latex]a_{2}=4[/latex], [latex]\therefore  \;\; f\left ( x \right )=1-x+4x^{2}[/latex] Now, exact value of [latex]\begin{aligned} &\int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx \\   &=\int_{0}^{2}\left ( 1-x+4x^{2} \right ) \\   &=\left [ x-\frac{x^{2}}{2}+\frac{4x^{3}}{3} \right ]_{0}^{2}=\frac{32}{3} \end{aligned}[/latex] Error = Exact-Approximate value [latex] =\frac{32}{3}-12=-\frac{4}{3}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
f(x)=1, 4, 15 at x=0, 1 and 2 respectively
[latex] \int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx =\frac{h}{2}\left ( f_{1}+2f_{2}+f_{3} \right ) [/latex](3 point Trapezoidal Rule)
Here h=1
[latex]\therefore \;\; \int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx=\left ( 1+2\times +15 \right )=12[/latex]
[latex]\therefore [/latex] Approximate value by Trapezoidal Rule =12
Since f(x) is second degree polynomial, let,
[latex] \begin{aligned} f\left ( x \right )&=a_{0}+a_{1}x+a_{2}x^{2} \\ f\left ( 0 \right )&=1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a_{0}+0+0&=1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a_{0}&=1 \\ f\left ( 1 \right )&=4 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a_{0}+a_{1}+a_{2}&=4 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; 1+a_{1}+a_{2}&=4 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a_{1}+a_{2}&=3 \;\;\;...(i)\\ f\left ( 2 \right )&=15 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a_{0}+2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=15 \\ \Rightarrow \;\;1+2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=15 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; 2a_{1}+4a_{2}&=14 \;\;\; ...(ii) \end{aligned}[/latex]
Solving (i) and (ii) [latex]a_{1}=-1[/latex] and [latex]a_{2}=4[/latex],
[latex]\therefore \;\; f\left ( x \right )=1-x+4x^{2}[/latex]
Now, exact value of
[latex]\begin{aligned} &\int_{0}^{2}f\left ( x \right )dx \\ &=\int_{0}^{2}\left ( 1-x+4x^{2} \right ) \\ &=\left [ x-\frac{x^{2}}{2}+\frac{4x^{3}}{3} \right ]_{0}^{2}=\frac{32}{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Error = Exact-Approximate value
[latex] =\frac{32}{3}-12=-\frac{4}{3}[/latex]

brake distance is 6:5. Considering total reaction time of the driver as 2.5 seconds

questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text { Lag distance } &=0.278 \mathrm{Vt} \\ &=0.278 \times 60 \times 2.5 \\ &=41.7 \mathrm{m} \\ \text { Brake distance }&=\frac{5}{6} \times 41.7=34.75 \mathrm{m} \\ &\left[\because \frac{\text { Lag distance }}{\text { Braking distance }}=\frac{6}{5}\right] \\ \text { Braking distance } &=\frac{V^{2}}{254(f+0.01 n)}\\ \Rightarrow \quad 34.75&=\frac{(60)^{2}}{254(0.36+0.01 n)} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.01 n&=\frac{(60)^{2}}{254 \times 34.75}-0.36 \\ \Rightarrow \quad n&=4.8 \% \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question:
In a rapid sand filter, the time for reaching particle break through ([latex]T_B[/latex]) is defined
as the time elapsed from start of filter run to the time at which the turbidity
of the effluent from the filter is greater than 2.5 NTU. The time for reaching
terminal head loss ([latex]T_H[/latex]) is defined as the time elapsed from the start of the filter
run to the time when head loss across the filter is greater than 3 m. The effect of increasing the filter depth (while keeping all other conditions same) on [latex]T_{B}[/latex] and [latex]T_{H}[/latex] is
questions.explanation: The effect of increase in certain rapid sand filter and influent particle characteristics on time ([latex]T_{B}[/latex]) for reaching particle breakthrough (turbidity [latex] \gt[/latex] 2.5 NTU) in the effluent, and time ([latex]T_{H}[/latex]) of reaching terminal head-loss([latex] \gt[/latex] 3 m) across filter bed are given below. Explain the results based on you understanding of filter operation and particle removal mechanisms operative in rapid sand filters. Assume that when one characteristic is changed, all other characteristic remain fixed. Effect of increase in filter depth (L) [latex]T_{B}[/latex] : [latex]T_{B}[/latex] will increase since particles in water will have the opportunity to potentially interact with more collectors, and hence the change for particle attachment to a collector is more. [latex]T_{H}[/latex]: Since bed depth is more, water is encounter more resistance is passing through the bed. Hence [latex]T_{H}[/latex] will decrease. Effect of increase in superdicial velocity ([latex]V_{s}[/latex]) [latex]T_{B}[/latex]: Since pore velocity is more, the shear forces experianced by collected particles will be more. Hence particle detachment will be more, leading to a decrease in [latex]T_{B}[/latex]. [latex]T_{H}[/latex]: Since particle loading rate on the filter and rate of particle collection in the filter will increase, the porosity of the filter bed will decrease more rapidly, leading to more rapid head-loss buildup and hence a decrease in [latex]T_{H}[/latex]. Effect of increase in influent particle concentration ([latex]C_{o}[/latex]) [latex]T_{B}[/latex]: Particle loading rate on the filter, rate of particle collection and hence porosity of the filter bed will decrease more rapidly. Thus pre velocity in the filter bed will increase more rapidly, leading to more rapid particle detachment. This will lead to decrease in [latex]T_{B}[/latex]. [latex]T_{H}[/latex]: Since particle loading rate on the filter and rate of particle collection in the filter will be increase, the porosity of the filter bed will decrease more rapidly, leading to more rapid head-loss buildup and hence a decrease in [latex]T_{H}[/latex].
